extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals (PRSA members and applicants) seeking the APR credential
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for earning and maintaining the Accreditation in Public Relations (APR), including application/candidacy, panel presentation, examination, and renewal. Includes resources and program variants (e.g., APR+M for military public affairs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: The APR is described as the profession’s gold standard — a mark of distinction that demonstrates strategic expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positioned as evidence that a candidate is strategic in approach to public relations; promoted through testimonials and program resources to help candidates demonstrate strategic thinking in their application, panel presentation and exam responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Accreditation demonstrates ethical practice as a core attribute of APR credential holders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethics is emphasized as part of what the APR signifies; resources and studies (e.g., boosting ethics counseling engagement) are provided to support candidates in demonstrating ethical practice during assessment and in professional development materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedication to lifelong learning / continuing professional development
rubrics_metrics.description: APR indicates a dedication to lifelong learning and ongoing professional growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates are expected to maintain expertise through renewal: track learning and growth, engage with PRSA resources, and use renewal guidance articles and tools to demonstrate continuing competency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge, skills and abilities (KSAs) / core competencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The accreditation assesses the knowledge, skills and abilities necessary for public relations practice; the Practice Examination covers these KSAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the APR Practice Examination and the Latest Practice Analysis (Identifying the Core Competencies Necessary in Public Relations Today) to identify and prepare the KSAs tested. PRSA offers study materials, webinars, and articles to align preparation with the identified core competencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel Presentation: demonstrated experience and presentation skills
rubrics_metrics.description: The Panel Presentation evaluates, through a questionnaire and a live presentation, knowledge, skills and abilities that cannot effectively be judged in the examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates should use the Panel Presentation Guide to assess their public relations experience and readiness to respond to the Panel Presentation Questionnaire before applying. PRSA provides webinars (e.g., 'APR Panel Presentation: Secrets to Success'), sample presentations, and boot camps to prepare. Emphasis is on real-world experience, clear presentation, and effective responses to panel questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination performance (online APR exam)
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must study for and pass the APR online examination, which tests aspects of PR knowledge and competencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRSA offers a Practice Examination, exam-day tips, webinars, and a Virtual Boot Camp to prepare. Members receive incentives (e.g., $100 rebate upon passing on first try). The exam complements the Panel Presentation by testing knowledge and judgment in formats suited to written/online assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application / candidacy eligibility and documentation of experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective candidates must apply for candidacy and document their public relations experience as part of the Accreditation process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use application resources and the Panel Presentation Guide to assess and document relevant experience before completing the application. PRSA provides an 'Apply Now' path and resources explaining candidacy requirements and preparation steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance/renewal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: After earning the APR, credential holders must maintain their expertise through renewal processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRSA provides guidance on making accreditation renewal simple, tracking learning and growth, and recommended activities to maintain the credential. Articles and tools explain renewal timelines and acceptable continuing professional development activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: APR+M (military public affairs specialization)
rubrics_metrics.description: A program variant — Accreditation in Public Relations + Military Communication (APR+M) — tailored for military public affairs professionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRSA offers APR+M-specific overviews and webinars (e.g., 'APR+M Process and Overview') to explain requirements and resources specific to military public affairs practitioners pursuing accreditation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership and mentorship as outcomes/expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The APR credential positions holders as leaders and mentors in the public relations field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRSA emphasizes leadership and mentoring in promotional language and testimonials; candidates and APRs are encouraged to demonstrate leadership, mentor others, and leverage the credential in career advancement and organizational roles.
